Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:33: After all this, the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on His creatures, as it is said (Isaiah 57:16) "for I will not contend forever, nor will I always be angry, for the spirit would faint before Me, and the souls I have made."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:35: In Midrash Ruth HaNe'elam (Zohar Chadash 79a), the seven chambers and what is punished in them are explained briefly - their words:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:36: The first chamber is called Bor [Pit], and it is the uppermost chamber, and there are several angels of destruction there, like a pit that has no water but has snakes and scorpions in it; so this chamber, called Bor, has several companies of angels of destruction like serpents and seraphim who have no charm against them. Three appointees rule in Gehinnom, and they are under the hand of Dumah - they are Mashchit [Destroyer], Af [Anger], and Cheimah [Fury], and all the others are appointed beneath them, and all these chambers run back and forth, judging the souls of the wicked there; and all these companies of angels of destruction all shake Gehinnom, and their voice is heard in the firmament, and the voice of the wicked among them cries out and says, "woe, woe," and no one has mercy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:37: He says afterward: in the first chamber they judge those who pick mallow-leaves from the bush [a euphemism for idle chatter], who interrupt words given on the tablets for idle chatter, and those who do not give honor to Torah scholars - though one who demeans Torah scholars is not judged in this place, but rather is judged in Tit HaYaven [Miry Clay] - and one who curses a deaf person and the like, and one who passes behind the synagogue while the congregation is praying, and one who tells his fellow's praise before someone who hates him for the worse [so that it provokes further hatred] - all these and the like are judged in the first chamber.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:38: The second chamber is called Shachat [Pit/Destruction], and it is a green fire, and there is nothing there but darkness, with no mercy at all; there they judge all who speak ill after the death of Torah scholars, one who shames his fellow in a matter of Jewish law so as not to learn from him, one who is proud not for the sake of Heaven, one who glorifies himself through his fellow's disgrace, one who knows his fellow will stumble in a matter of law - both being in the same town - and does not inform him before he stumbles, and rejoices, he or others; and one who has a synagogue in his town and does not enter to pray there; and one who is not accommodating to his fellow in a matter of law, both being in the same town; and one who eats from a meal that is insufficient for its host; and one who raises his hand against his fellow even though he did not strike him; and one who curses his fellow in jest in a way that brings him shame - all these are judged in this chamber, and all like them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:39: Concerning what he said, "one who knows his fellow will stumble in a matter of law and does not inform him," Rashbi tells (Shelach 167a) that a certain sage did this to his fellow, and it says there, concerning the souls that would come to Rashbi, peace be upon him, to tell him of the words of the Garden of Eden and supernal secrets: meanwhile one flew away and was hidden from them, and after a while returned to them. He said to them, "I was invited to enter, and they were all in a single crown, judging the case of a certain person who stood at the gate of the Garden of Eden, and the cherubs held him and did not let him enter there, and he was in distress among them, and cried out at the gate, and all the righteous there heard it, and now all the members of the academy are gathering to go before the Messiah King, to examine his case." And they told afterward his punishment, and said: "the judgment they judged him and the Messiah decreed was that this person be left outside, in that distress, for forty days; at the end of forty days they would afflict him with the distress of Gehinnom for an hour and a half. And all this because one day one of the colleagues had been expounding words of Torah, and when he reached a certain point he knew that this person would stumble on it, and he said to the colleagues, 'be silent, do not say anything,' and because the colleagues were silent, this person stumbled on that point and was embarrassed; and that embarrassment which this person caused is why he is judged with this harsh judgment, since the Holy One, blessed be He, does not wish to let the joy of Torah be withheld even by a hair's breadth" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:40: Along these lines, it is explained there (171b) concerning a certain child who shamed his teacher with questions, and was punished - his words: "and because they wished to judge his case openly, he was saved from it, since he had shamed his teacher before everyone with his questions and difficulties, and did not take care to go elsewhere to prepare his studies, and weakened his teacher's spirit; and because they did not wish to judge him with harsh judgment - therefore, even though he was saved from the Master of Judgment, he was not saved here: seven days his image was not completed here, and he would be immersed with extra pain before everyone all those seven days, until his image was completed" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:41: The third chamber is called Dumah, and there are judged all those coarse of spirit whose hearts are proud in matters of law before the people, not for the sake of Heaven, and those who speak slander, and one whose heart is proud in giving rulings, and one who judges his fellow to the side of guilt, and one who lends to his fellow with interest, and one who shows a false face in [teaching] Torah, not according to law, and one who does not answer "Amen" to the one reciting a blessing, and one who makes a "break" - such as one who speaks during his prayer, and repeats and says something else, and interrupts again, and is called a "breaker" - and one who mocks his fellow or an elder who has forgotten his learning, and one who sees a matter of impropriety in his fellow and does not inform him privately - all these are judged there, and all like them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:42: The fourth chamber is called Tit HaYaven [Miry Clay]; there are judged those coarse of spirit, and all who answer the poor and the downtrodden with insolence, and one who sees a poor person in distress and does not lend to him until he seeks his own benefit from it, and one who withholds a hired worker's wages, and one who emits seed in vain, and one who has relations with a gentile woman or a menstruant, and one who takes a pledge from a poor man and does not return his pledges when he has nothing else, and one who perverts justice, and one who takes a bribe - all are judged in this chamber.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:43: The fifth chamber is called Sheol; there are judged informers, heretics, deniers of the Torah, and deniers of the resurrection of the dead, and of them it is said (Job 7:9) "as a cloud fades away and vanishes, so he who goes down to Sheol does not come up." But of the other sinners it is written (I Samuel 2:6) "the Lord kills and makes alive, brings down to Sheol and brings up."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:44: The sixth chamber is Tzalmavet [Shadow of Death]; there are judged all those who lay with their mothers, and with a menstruant.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:45: The seventh chamber is Eretz Tachtit [Lowest Land]; whoever descends there no longer comes up, as it is said (Malachi 3:21) "and you shall trample the wicked," etc.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:46: In the Zohar (Terumah 150b) it says there is a place in Gehinnom called "boiling filth," where all those who sinned and caused the multitude to sin are judged, and likewise those who emit seed in vain deliberately - his words: "there is a place in Gehinnom, and levels there, called 'boiling filth,' and there is the impurity of souls who were sullied with all the impurity of this world, who are refined and ascend, and that impurity remains there; and those evil levels called 'boiling filth' are appointed over that impurity, and the fire of Gehinnom rules over that remaining impurity. And there are wicked ones who are constantly sullied by their sins and are not refined of them, and die without repentance - those who sinned and caused others to sin, and were always stiff-necked and never broken before their Master in this world - these are judged there in that impurity and in that boiling filth, and never come out of there forever; those who ruin their ways on earth and did not care for the honor of their Master in this world, all of them are judged there for generations upon generations and never come out from there. On Sabbaths and New Moons and appointed times and festivals, the fire in that place subsides and they are not judged, but they still do not come out of there, unlike other wicked ones who have rest" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:47: He says afterward that one who profanes the Sabbath in public is judged forever, even on the Sabbath, and the other wicked who kept the Sabbath go out to see the judgment of these who did not keep the Sabbath, and of them it is said (Isaiah 66:24) "and they shall go out and look upon the corpses of the men who transgressed against Me, for their worm shall not die, nor their fire be quenched, and they shall be an abhorrence to all flesh." "For their worm shall not die" - from the body; "nor their fire be quenched" - from the soul; and they explain, what is "an abhorrence" [dera'on]? "Enough seeing" [dei re'iyah] - for all the wicked say, "enough of this sight."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:48: In the Tikkunim (49b), it explains there that there is a Gehinnom for nefesh, ruach, and neshamah, which are called "the candle of the Lord is the soul of man," and it says that "Ne"R" [candle] stands for Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, and it says: whoever keeps "the candle of the Lord is the soul of man" in the Torah, in the positive and negative commandments, the fire of Gehinnom has no power over him; and this corresponds to liver, gall, and spleen - liver is red fire, gall is green fire, spleen is black fire, and the fatty lobe is the sum of all of them, dark blue - so far. And it says further on there, gall, liver, and spleen are the exile for neshamah, ruach, and nefesh - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:49: I have chosen to copy here for you the seven Palaces of Impurity that Rabbi Shimon brought in the portion of Pekudei, and my teacher, peace be upon him, copied them in the Sefer HaPardes in the holy tongue, and therefore I shall quote his words:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:50: In the first Palace, called Bor [Pit] - and the pit is empty, and whoever comes to enter it has no support to hold onto so as not to fall, but they all push him so that he falls into it. In this Palace one appointee, named Dumah, stands, and he stands at the entrance of the first Palace of Holiness from outside, with several angels of destruction, to seize the souls that the holy angel Bohariel pushes away, as explained in the Gate of the Holy Palaces, chapter 1.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:51: Beneath this appointee, Dumah, there is another appointee named Patut, and beneath his hand are several thousand and myriad angels of destruction, and he is appointed to entice human beings from the good way, to gaze upon adultery and lewdness - as his name, so is his action. And all the angels of destruction with him go before human beings to keep their eyes on transgression. This appointee is also called Sarsurim, for he is the broker of transgression, and this appointee stands over the grave at the time the body is judged, and shatters its eyes, because it inclined after his counsel, for such is the way of the kelipah - to accuse below, and ascend and accuse above, and descend and take its soul, and whoever is drawn after him takes his own revenge upon himself.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:52: Within this Palace are several serpents and scorpions that bite the soul when it enters there. Over this whole Palace one appointee stands, named Gimguma, and he is red as a rose, and he stands to accuse when a person's prayer is rejected from the first Palace of Holiness, as I explained in the Gate of Palaces, chapter 1; and when this one receives that rejected prayer, it ascends with him to the seventh Palace of the kelipah, and from there he teaches guilt against him and mentions his sins - this is what Scripture says (Job 1:6) "and Satan also came" - "also" [gam] hints at the name of this Satan, who is Gimguma.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:53: Beneath his hand are several angels of destruction appointed to seize all vile or blemished words a person utters with his lips, and they preserve them; and when the person then utters words of holiness with his mouth, such as words of Torah or prayer, they defile those holy words with that impurity he had uttered from his mouth beforehand, and then, as it were, the power of holiness is weakened - and woe, woe to the soul of that sinner.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:54: Further, in this Palace, over all these appointees is one appointee, named Tafsurinia, and beneath his hand are several angels of destruction, appointed over everything a person throws in anger from his hand; they take that object and bring it up above, and say, "this is an offering of so-and-so, which was offered to us," and they proclaim and say, "woe to so-and-so, who has strayed after a foreign god," and a Heavenly Voice goes forth a second time and says, "woe to them, for they have strayed from Me." This Palace is called Satan Bor.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:55: The second Palace is called Shachat, and it is impure and dark. This Palace has three gates on three sides. At the first gate stands one appointee, named Eshtariah, and beneath his hand several thousand and myriad appointees, and they are appointed over those who emit seed in vain, who do not see the face of the Shechinah; these come and defile him in this world, and afterward, when his soul departs, they seize him and bring him in to be judged among them; these are called "boiling seed," and they take the heat of the transgression and the seed and bring it up above, and cause the holy covenant to be subjugated beneath the kelipot.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:56: At the second gate is one appointee, named Taskifa, appointed over all those who have relations with animals or with the severe forbidden relations of the Torah, and beneath his hand several thousand and myriad angels of destruction, whose way with this man is like the way of those mentioned above.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:57: In this Palace there is one appointee named Kos HaTar'elah [the Cup of Poison], and all those executed by the court who drank the cup of poison in this world are saved from the cup of poison of the World to Come. What is the cup of poison? At the departure of the soul from the body, this appointee, called the Cup of Poison, seizes him and gives him to drink from the cup of poison; and in this cup there are three drops - one gravel, one "more bitter than death," and one "cupping." In this Palace stands one appointee, named Otzi Ariel, and from there they give him drink on the day of death - this is the "three drops of the sword of the Angel of Death" that our Sages, of blessed memory, mentioned.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:58: At the third gate is one appointee, named Sangadiel, appointed over all those who bring in and defile their covenant with the daughter of a foreign god, and all those who defile themselves with a gentile woman; here are depicted the images of the women with whom they defiled themselves, at this appointee's hand, and several thousand appointees are beneath his hand; and when his soul departs, they defile it with that image and it becomes bound with him in the Palace - this is what our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Sotah 3b) on "and he did not listen to her, to lie beside her, to be with her" (Genesis 39:10) - "to lie beside her" in this world, "to be with her" bound in the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:59: Within this Palace is one impure spirit, in whom hang all sorceries and all kinds of divinations, and they all hang on the impurity of "boiling seed" - this was the wisdom of Balaam the wicked, who would defile himself with his donkey and thereby succeed in his sorceries; and for this reason this Palace is called "impure Shachat," for "impure" it is, "impure" it shall be called.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:60: Beneath this upper spirit there is in this Palace yet another impure spirit, named Sartiah, and several thousand and myriad angels of destruction beneath him, and they are ready at the time a dream descends from the side of holiness - this spirit and all the angels of destruction with him descend with that dream and mix with it, and make known to that man words of folly mixed with the true dream; and so [it explains] the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, that just as it is impossible for grain to be without straw, so it is impossible for a dream to be without idle words.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:61: From the side of this Palace go forth two spirits, sometimes transforming into men and sometimes into women; and when the supernal impure spirits travel, from the side of their travel two flames and blazes come into being and go forth and spread through the world, and appear to human beings in dreams in the likeness of beautiful women, and defile them with a seminal emission; all this is drawn after their own words, drawing their spirit upon himself through his deeds. This is what the Torah says (Deuteronomy 23:10) "and you shall guard yourself from every evil thing," as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain, that one should not have improper thoughts by day, lest he come to impurity at night, God forbid.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:62: Concerning this matter it is explained in the Zohar, portion of Terumah (130a) - his words: "one appointee stands for that secret, over that female of the north, among all those bundles of impure spirits - his name is Sanugiriya - and at the time that smoke bends its way and ascends, this appointee and sixty thousand myriad other camps, all prepare to receive it and be nourished from it, and stand by that female, and enter through one gate called Keri [seminal emission], and this is the secret, as it is written (Leviticus 26:21) 'and if you walk with Me as chance [keri]...' - 'then I too will walk with you' - 'in the fury of chance' - in that wrath that goes forth from the gate of Keri; and these are the ones that roam by night, and at the time souls go forth to ascend to be seen above, these go forth and accuse them so they cannot ascend, except for those holy pious ones who cleave the firmaments and airs and ascend. And these bundles of impure spirits go forth and make false things known to human beings and appear to them in other images and laugh at them until they emit seed, and are called 'masters of chance,' because they go forth through the gate of Keri, which they cause. And at the time the sacrificial portions and fats are consumed [on the altar], that smoke gives them drink and nourishes them according to their honor - such is their food, as is fitting for them - and thereby they do not go forth and roam through the Holy Land" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:63: And what he says, "that smoke bends," is explained above this passage, but we have not written it; its meaning is that in the morning Tamid offering and the afternoon Tamid offering the wind did not overcome the pillar of smoke, but at night the smoke would of itself bend toward the north, so that those masters of Keri would be nourished from it, so that they would not roam through the Land of Israel. Concerning the matter of one who has a seminal emission, it is further explained in the Zohar, portion of Bereishit (19b, 55a), see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:64: The third Palace is called the Palace of Ofel [Gloom], and it is darker and gloomier than the previous ones, and it is called Dumah, for although we said that he descends to the first Palace, his essence is in this Palace, and correspondingly the evil inclination is called "enemy."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:65: This Palace has four gates, and over them four appointees, as we shall explain. At the first gate is one appointee, named Katratia, and he stands in the power of wrath when judgment is stretched over the world, and this is the downfall of the wicked; concerning this it is said (Proverbs 4:19) "the way of the wicked is like darkness; they do not know at what they stumble." This appointee stands at the crossroads to trip up, with his plague, those who travel alone on the roads and in the marketplaces, and can harm them if he encounters them - and this is when he rules in the world through the strength of stretched-out judgment, God forbid.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:66: At the second gate is one appointee named Sangadiel (variant: Hangariel), and beneath his hand several thousand and myriad angels of destruction, and they all stand to receive the notes of judgment from outside the third Palace, the Palace of Holiness. And when he receives the notes of judgment, he descends to the two previous Palaces, Shachat and Bor, and there he has several thousand and myriad angels of destruction, and they all roam through the world to complete that judgment, God forbid.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:67: At the third gate is one appointee, named Angiriyahun, and he is appointed over all the burning fevers within the bones, and all kinds of evil diseases that burn and consume the body, and from him go forth several thousand and myriad appointees over this same matter, like him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:68: At the fourth gate is one appointee, named Askarah [croup], appointed over the killing and death of infants up to the age of thirteen, and he appears as a woman who raises and nurses them and plays with them and strangles them, and their soul is delivered into the hand of the angel Azriel in the third Palace of holiness, as explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:69: In the middle of this Palace stands one spirit, called Agirision, and he is appointed over the death of young men from the age of thirteen to twenty, of whom it is said (Proverbs 13:23) "and there is one swept away without justice" - for since they are not guarded when they are young because of their poor upbringing, and he sees in them a sign that they will sin and be corrupted, he kills them before they come to sin; concerning this it is said (Genesis 1:31) "and behold, it was very good" [tov me'od] - this is the Angel of Death [understood as a hint: tov mot].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:70: From this Palace two spirits spread out, named Af [Anger] and Cheimah [Fury], and these Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, saw when he descended from the mountain, and said (Deuteronomy 9:19) "for I was in dread of the anger and the fury," and beneath their hand several thousand and myriad angels of destruction, and they are all appointed over all those who hear a ban or excommunication from the mouth of a Torah master and do not take it to heart, and likewise over all those who mock words of Torah or the sages; and so they all go about to provoke all those who occupy themselves with Torah, and likewise with the performance of a mitzvah, so that they should not rejoice in it but be saddened by it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:71: Beneath these spirits is one spirit, named Sichsicha, and when a person slanders his fellow or stirs up strife against him, this one is aroused with that slander to complete the matter and to kill through that slander.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 13:72: Come and see: although the Holy One, blessed be He, established a set time for all beasts and serpents to shed their skin, nevertheless everything depends on slander and gossip - when a person slanders his fellow, the lower beasts shed their skin and give voices, and those voices ascend above to the Palace called Bor, where there are several serpents and scorpions, as I explained above, and they all teach a case for provocation, to arouse the primordial serpent, the great serpent, and he sheds his skin, and all his bows - meaning his camps and hosts - separate from him, and he sends them down below into the Palaces, and he ascends to speak provocation with that slander; and were it not for the shedding of his skin, no one could stand before him - may the Merciful One save us - and all this because of the strength of slander and gossip, and it was not for nothing that our Sages, of blessed memory, said that it is a graver transgression than sexual immorality, idolatry, and bloodshed.
